title: Checkpoint: What Makes an Animal
objective: After this level you can sort animals by backbone, body temperature and diet.
summary: Three questions sort most animals: backbone or not, inside or outside heat, and what it eats. Some answers change with age: gray tree frog tadpoles eat algae and debris, while adults eat insects.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: three questions sort almost any animal.
cards.body: Does it have a backbone? Does it make its own heat? What does it eat? This chapter gave you all three. Let's run a few animals through them, then meet one that changes an answer halfway through its life.

cards.fact: A gray tree frog switches diets as it grows up.
cards.context: As tadpoles, gray tree frogs eat algae and bits of rotting debris in the water. Adults mainly hunt insects and their larvae. So the diet question depends on when you ask: algae and debris when young, insects when grown. The other two answers never change. A frog is an amphibian, so it has a backbone, and it takes its heat from outside.

mascot.line: Salad as a kid, bugs as a grown-up. Every frog has a coming-of-age story.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: What makes something an animal, and why a sponge that never moves as an adult still counts.
Why most animal species are still unnamed, and how scientists estimate the ones nobody has found.
How a backbone, body heat and diet sort almost any animal into its group.
Why energy thins out up a food chain, and how one predator can hold a whole ecosystem together.

questions.prompt: What Makes an Animal recap: which set of labels fits the ochre sea star?
